title.en: The Pygmy of the Dances: Pepi II Sends for a Dwarf of the God
title.zh: 舞神之侏儒：佩皮二世迎矮人

region.en: Aswan, Egypt (tomb of Herkhuf, the caravan-governor) and the Land of the Spirits far south
region.zh: 埃及阿斯旺（赫爾庫夫之墓）與極南『神靈之地』

texts.period: Royal despatch of Pepi II, year 2, 6th Dynasty (c. 2278 BCE); cut on the facade of Herkhuf's tomb (Budge translation 1910)

source.work: The Literature of the Ancient Egyptians, trans. E. A. W. Budge (1910), ch. IX, the Autobiography of Herkhuf and the letter of Pepi II

summary.en: The oldest piece of royal correspondence on earth: Herkhuf writes from the far south that he has brought back a pygmy 'who can dance the dance of the god, from the Land of the Spirits, like the pygmy whom the seal-bearer of the god Baurtet brought back from Punt in the time of Assa' — and the child-king Pepi II replies that he longs to see the pygmy 'more than any offering of the countries of Ba and Punt', with orders that trustworthy men sleep beside him ten times a night lest he fall into the water.
summary.zh: 世上最古之王家書信：赫爾庫夫自極南奏報，已自『神靈之地』攜回『能舞神舞』之侏儒，如阿薩王時神之印吏自彭特攜回者；幼王佩皮二世覆書：朕欲見此侏儒之心，勝於巴與彭特一切貢品——並敕可靠者守於其側，夜察十次，恐其墜水。

sensitivity.note: Ancient royal letter via Budge 1910; no living community restrictions. 'Land of the Spirits' (Ta-Neter) is the Egyptian name for the far-southern divine lands; the pygmy was regarded as a being of the god's own country.

passages.text: Thou sayest in this thy letter that there hath been brought back by thee [also] a pygmy (or dwarf) who can dance the dance of the god, from the Land of the Spirits, like the pygmy whom the seal-bearer of the god Baurtet brought back from Punt in the time of Assa. Thou sayest to [my] Majesty, 'The like of him hath never been brought back by any other person who hath visited Amam.' Behold, every year thou performest what thy Lord wisheth and praiseth.
passages.note: Verbatim excerpt of Budge, Literature of the Ancient Egyptians (1910), ch. IX, the letter of Pepi II.

passages.text: Come down the river at once to the Capital. Bring with thee this pygmy whom thou hast brought from the Land of the Spirits, alive, strong, and healthy, to dance the dance of the god, and to cheer and gratify the heart of the King of the South and North, Neferkara, the everliving. When he cometh down with thee in the boat, cause trustworthy men to be about him on both sides of the boat, to prevent him from falling into the water. When he is asleep at night cause trustworthy men to sleep by his side on his bedding. See [that he is there] ten times [each] night. [My] Majesty wisheth to see this pygmy more than any offering of the countries of Ba and Punt.
passages.note: Verbatim excerpt of Budge (1910), ch. IX.

passages.text: If when thou arrivest at the Capital, this pygmy who is with thee is alive, and strong, and in good health, [My] Majesty will confer upon thee a greater honour than that which was conferred upon the bearer of the seal Baurtet in the time of Assa, and as great is the wish of [My] Majesty to see this pygmy orders have been brought to the smer, the overseer of the priests, the governor of the town ... to arrange that rations for him shall be drawn from every station of supply, and from every temple.
passages.note: Verbatim excerpt of Budge (1910), ch. IX.

title.en: Una Alone in the Hall: The Secret Inquiry into the Chief Wife
title.zh: 烏納獨任推事：王后密案之審

region.en: Abydos, Egypt (tomb stele of Una, judge belonging to Nekhen)
region.zh: 埃及阿拜多斯（烏納墓碑，奈肯之判官）

texts.period: 6th Dynasty (reigns of Teta, Pepi I, Merenra); stele now in Cairo (Budge translation 1910)

source.work: The Literature of the Ancient Egyptians, trans. E. A. W. Budge (1910), ch. IX, the Autobiography of Una

summary.en: A harem drama of the 6th Dynasty, told in stone: when a secret inquiry was opened in the royal household concerning the Chief Wife Amtes, King Pepi made the estate-overseer Una hear the case by himself — no Chief Justice, no town governor, no nobleman, only a man of middle rank 'because the heart of His Majesty was filled with me' — and Una wrote the judgment alone, a thing never before done for a man of his rank.
summary.zh: 第六王朝宮闈劇，刻於石上：王后阿姆特斯之密案起，王命田莊督烏納獨任聽審——無大法官、無城守、無貴族在座——僅以中級官員一人，『因王心為我所充滿』；烏納獨自錄其判詞——同僚位者未嘗有此。

sensitivity.note: Ancient autobiographical inscription via Budge 1910; no living community restrictions.

passages.text: His Majesty made me a 'judge belonging to Nekhen.' His heart was more satisfied with me than with any other of his servants. Alone I heard every kind of private case, there being with me only the Chief Justice and the Governor of the town ... in the name of the king, of the royal household, and of the Six Great Houses.
passages.note: Verbatim excerpt of Budge, Literature of the Ancient Egyptians (1910), ch. IX, the Autobiography of Una.

passages.text: During the secret inquiry which was made in the king's household concerning the Chief Wife Amtes, His Majesty made me enter to hear the case by myself. There was no Chief Justice there, and no Town Governor, and no nobleman, only myself, and this was because I was able and acceptable to the heart of His Majesty, and because the heart of His Majesty was filled with me. I did the case into writing, I alone, with only one judge belonging to Nekhen, and yet my rank was only that of overseer of the estates of Pharaoh. Never before did a man of my rank hear the case of a secret of the royal household.
passages.note: Verbatim excerpt of Budge (1910), ch. IX.

passages.text: This army returned in peace, having raided the Land of the dwellers on sand. This army returned in peace, having thrown down the fortresses thereof. This army returned in peace, having cut down its fig-trees and vines. This army returned in peace, having set fire [to the temples] of all its gods. This army returned in peace, having slain the soldiers there in many tens of thousands. This army returned in peace, bringing back with it vast numbers of the fighting men thereof as living prisoners. His Majesty praised me for this exceedingly.
passages.note: Verbatim excerpt of Budge (1910), ch. IX, Una's five campaigns at the head of the army.
